questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following schematics correctly depict a lac operon that can be negatively regulated?
questions.solution:
For a lac operon to be negatively regulated, the repressor protein (synthesized by the regulatory gene $i$) must be able to bind to the operator (O$) and block RNA polymerase from transcribing the structural genes.

This mechanism requires the operator (O$) to be located immediately downstream of the promoter (P$) for the structural genes, so that repressor binding physically obstructs transcription.

Evaluating the given schematics:
In schematic (i), the arrangement is $P-i-P-O-z-y-a$. The operator $O$ is correctly positioned between the second promoter $P$ and the structural genes $z, y, a$. This allows for negative regulation.

In schematic (ii), the operator $O$ is placed upstream of the $i$ gene, and the structural genes are separated by another promoter. This does not allow coordinated negative regulation of the structural genes.

In schematic (iii), the arrangement is $P-i-P-O-y-z-a$. Although the order of the structural genes is altered, the operator $O$ is still correctly positioned immediately downstream of the promoter $P$. The repressor can still bind to $O$ and block transcription of the structural genes. Thus, it can be negatively regulated.

In schematic (iv), the arrangement is $P-O-i-P-z-y-a$. The operator $O$ is upstream of the $i$ gene. The structural genes $z, y, a$ have a promoter $P$ but lack an adjacent operator to block their transcription, meaning they would be constitutively expressed.

Therefore, schematics (i) and (iii) correctly depict an operon that can be negatively regulated.

Answer: i and iii$

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of the coding strand of the given gene?
questions.solution:
According to the convention, the promoter is located towards the 5' end of the coding strand.

In the given figure, the promoter is present on the right side. The bottom strand has its 5' end on the right side. Thus, the bottom strand acts as the coding strand.

Alternatively, the arrow for the transcription start site indicates that transcription proceeds from right to left. RNA polymerase reads the template strand in the 3' \rightarrow 5' direction. The top strand has its 3' end on the right, so it serves as the template strand. Consequently, the bottom strand is the coding strand.

The sequence of a DNA strand is conventionally written in the 5' \rightarrow 3' direction.

Reading the bottom strand from the 5' end (right) to the 3' end (left), the sequence is:
5' GTGCTGTAACGGCTTCAC 3'.

Answer: 5' GTGCTGTAACGGCTTCAC 3'
